name: Human brain (MEG signal)
citation: Hamalainen M. et al. (1993) Magnetoencephalography: theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain. Rev Mod Phys 65, 413
notes: Femtotesla to picotesla at the scalp

name: Interstellar magnetic field
citation: Ferriere K.M. (2001) The interstellar environment of our galaxy. Rev Mod Phys 73, 1031

name: Earth's surface field
citation: Alken P. et al. (2021) International Geomagnetic Reference Field: the thirteenth generation. Earth Planets Space 73, 49

name: Sunspot
citation: Solanki S.K. (2003) Sunspots: an overview of observational evidence. A&A Rev 11, 153
notes: Umbral fields of a few kilogauss

name: MRI scanner
citation: Boulant N. et al. (2024) In vivo imaging of the human brain with the Iseult 11.7-T MRI scanner. Nature Methods 21, 2013

name: Strongest continuous lab field
citation: Hahn S. et al. (2019) 45.5-tesla direct-current magnetic field generated with a high-temperature superconducting magnet. Nature 570, 496

name: Strongest indoor pulsed field
citation: Nakamura D. et al. (2018) Record indoor magnetic field of 1200 T generated by electromagnetic flux-compression. Rev Sci Instrum 89, 095106

name: Magnetic white dwarfs
citation: Ferrario L., de Martino D. & Gansicke B.T. (2015) Magnetic white dwarfs. Space Sci Rev 191, 111

name: Radio pulsars
citation: Manchester R.N. et al. (2005) The Australia Telescope National Facility pulsar catalogue. AJ 129, 1993

name: Magnetars
citation: Olausen S.A. & Kaspi V.M. (2014) The McGill magnetar catalog. ApJS 212, 6
notes: SGR 1806-20 near 2e11 T: above the quantum critical field

name: Heavy-ion collision (gold or lead nuclei)
citation: Skokov V., Illarionov A.Yu. & Toneev V. (2009) Estimate of the magnetic field strength in heavy-ion collisions. Int J Mod Phys A 24, 5925
notes: eB from 0.1 m_pi^2 (SPS) to about 1 m_pi^2 (RHIC) and 15 m_pi^2 (LHC): the strongest fields in the universe

name: Petawatt laser hitting a solid
citation: Tatarakis M. et al. (2002) Measuring huge magnetic fields. Nature 415, 280
notes: More than 340 megagauss in the dense plasma for about a picosecond (size approximate)

name: Neodymium magnet
citation: Sagawa M. et al. (1984) New material for permanent magnets on a base of Nd and Fe. J Appl Phys 55, 2083
notes: Remanence about 1.2 T: the strongest permanent magnets

name: Human heart (magnetocardiogram)
citation: Cohen D. (1967) Magnetic fields around the torso: production by electrical activity of the human heart. Science 156, 652
notes: Tens of picotesla: a hundred times the brain's signal

name: Earth's outer core
citation: Gillet N. et al. (2010) Fast torsional waves and strong magnetic field within the Earth's core. Nature 465, 74
notes: About 4 mT inside the core: 80 times the surface field

name: Jupiter's surface field
citation: Connerney J.E.P. et al. (2018) A new model of Jupiter's magnetic field from Juno's first nine orbits. GRL 45, 2590
notes: About 4 gauss at the equator: the strongest planetary field

name: Solar wind at Earth's orbit
citation: Owens M.J. & Forsyth R.J. (2013) The heliospheric magnetic field. Living Rev Sol Phys 10, 5
notes: About 5 nT carried out by the solar wind

name: Galaxy cluster
citation: Carilli C.L. & Taylor G.B. (2002) Cluster magnetic fields. ARA&A 40, 319
notes: A few microgauss across a megaparsec of hot gas

name: Intergalactic voids (lower bound)
citation: Neronov A. & Vovk I. (2010) Evidence for strong extragalactic magnetic fields from Fermi observations of TeV blazars. Science 328, 73
notes: At least 3e-16 gauss: inferred from missing GeV cascades of TeV blazars
